
Setup plan: Qwen3.6 35B-A3B (Q4_K_M, 22.1 GB) with llama.cpp (llama-server), tuned settings
  runtime chosen: the fastest working option here; not installed yet
  context 65536 tokens · 16-bit context cache · serves at http://127.0.0.1:8080 as "qwen3.6:35b-a3b-cyrlm"
  expected: first reply 11 s, then ~1.9 s per turn, writing at 188 tok/s
  ✓ Codex CLI connects through `cyrlm bridge`, which passes its requests to llama.cpp (llama-server)'s Chat Completions API at http://127.0.0.1:8080 as model qwen3.6:35b-a3b-cyrlm.

Nothing has been run. Run each step yourself (or let your coding agent run them, with your approval):

1. Check what is already installed
   cyrlm did not find llama.cpp (llama-server). These read-only commands confirm what is installed and running, and that there is room for the 22.1 GB download. A failing version command means the runtime is not installed or not on PATH.
     PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH" llama-server --version
     curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8080/health
     codex --version
     df -h "$HOME"

2. Install llama.cpp
   Downloads the newest prebuilt release for your backend (assets are named llama-<build>-bin-ubuntu-<backend>-<arch>.tar.gz; CUDA builds come in two CUDA versions, each with a cudart-… tarball of CUDA runtime libraries; this takes the highest version and extracts both. The newest CUDA needs a recent NVIDIA driver; if llama-server finds no CUDA device, use the older CUDA assets or build from source) into ~/.local/share/llama.cpp and links llama-server and llama-cli into ~/.local/bin. They are built on Ubuntu; on other distributions, or if a library is missing, build from source instead (cmake -B build -DGGML_CUDA=ON && cmake --build build --config Release) or use `brew install llama.cpp`.
     set -e
     dir="$HOME/.local/share/llama.cpp"; mkdir -p "$dir" "$HOME/.local/bin"
     url=$(curl -fsSL 'https://api.github.com/repos/ggml-org/llama.cpp/releases?per_page=5' | grep -oE '"browser_download_url": *"[^"]+"' | cut -d'"' -f4 | grep -E '/llama-[^/]*-bin-ubuntu-cuda-[0-9.]+-x64\.tar\.gz$' | sort -V | tail -n 1)
     [ -n "$url" ] || { echo "no matching release asset; pick one from https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/releases" >&2; exit 1; }
     curl -fL "$url" | tar -xz -C "$dir" --strip-components=1
     ver=$(echo "$url" | sed -E 's/.*-cuda-([0-9.]+)-.*/\1/')
     rt=$(curl -fsSL 'https://api.github.com/repos/ggml-org/llama.cpp/releases?per_page=5' | grep -oE '"browser_download_url": *"[^"]+"' | cut -d'"' -f4 | grep -E "/cudart-[^/]*-cuda-$ver-x64\.tar\.gz$" | sort -V | tail -n 1)
     [ -z "$rt" ] || curl -fL "$rt" | tar -xz -C "$dir" --strip-components=1
     ln -sf "$dir/llama-server" "$dir/llama-cli" "$HOME/.local/bin/"
     "$dir/llama-server" --version

3. Download Qwen3.6 35B-A3B Q4_K_M (22.1 GB) and test-load it  [downloads 22.1 GB]
   `-hf unsloth/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-GGUF:UD-Q4_K_M` downloads exactly the Q4_K_M GGUF (22.1 GB) from Hugging Face into llama.cpp's model cache (set LLAMA_CACHE to move it; HF_TOKEN for gated repos), the same cache `llama-server -hf` uses, then loads it and generates one token to prove the build and GPU backend work (the answer itself is checked later by `cyrlm verify`). --no-mmproj skips the optional vision projector (~1 GB more), which a text coding setup does not need. The download can take a while and may print little progress; the file grows under ~/.cache/llama.cpp or the Hugging Face cache.
     PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH" llama-cli -hf unsloth/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-GGUF:UD-Q4_K_M --no-mmproj -c 4096 -n 1 -st -p Hi

4. Write the llama-server launch script
   Keeps the tuned flags in one place so the server can be restarted the same way: -c 65536 sets the context window (otherwise it is sized to free memory or taken from the model); -fa on forces flash attention; --jinja uses the model's chat template (needed for tool calls); --no-mmproj skips the vision projector; -np 1 keeps one slot, so one coding session gets the whole context and the prompt cache; -ngl 999 offloads every layer to the GPU; --alias names the model qwen3.6:35b-a3b-cyrlm. Recent builds listen on port 9931 by default, so the port is set explicitly (8080).
   Create ~/.cyrlm/llamacpp/qwen3.6-35b-a3b-cyrlm.sh:
     #!/bin/sh
     # Generated by cyrlm plan: Qwen3.6 35B-A3B Q4_K_M on llama.cpp (cuda).
     PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"
     exec llama-server -hf unsloth/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-GGUF:UD-Q4_K_M -c 65536 -fa on --jinja --no-mmproj -np 1 -ngl 999 --alias qwen3.6:35b-a3b-cyrlm --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8080

5. Start llama-server on port 8080
   Starts the launch script detached (log: ~/.cyrlm/llamacpp/qwen3.6-35b-a3b-cyrlm.log) and returns once /health reports the model is loaded, so the server keeps running after this command returns. Run the undo command to stop it; run the start command again after a reboot.
     cyrlm bg --log "$HOME/.cyrlm/llamacpp/qwen3.6-35b-a3b-cyrlm.log" --ready http://127.0.0.1:8080/health -- sh "$HOME/.cyrlm/llamacpp/qwen3.6-35b-a3b-cyrlm.sh"

6. Start the Codex CLI bridge
   Codex sends requests that local runtimes' own Responses endpoints do not fully handle (namespaced tools, several developer messages, hosted web search; llama.cpp skips namespace tools and strict chat templates reject a second system message). `cyrlm bridge` accepts Codex CLI's requests on port 11535 (or the next free port) and passes them to http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1/chat/completions, the runtime's most mature API, with system messages merged for the model's chat template and tool calls mapped back; runtime errors are shown in Codex CLI instead of being retried. It returns once it answers and prints the exact Codex CLI command.
     cyrlm bridge --endpoint http://127.0.0.1:8080 --model qwen3.6:35b-a3b-cyrlm --harness codex --ctx 65536 --background

7. Start Codex CLI with qwen3.6:35b-a3b-cyrlm
   Everything is passed with -c overrides, so no Codex config file is edited, plain `codex` keeps working as before, and nothing depends on Codex's config layout (profiles moved to separate files in 0.134). Use the command the bridge printed: it has the real port and, when codex is not on your terminal's PATH, its full path. Web search is off because a local model cannot run OpenAI's hosted search.
     /Applications/ChatGPT.app/Contents/Resources/codex-cli/CodexCLI.app/Contents/MacOS/codex -c model_providers.cyrlm.name=cyrlm -c model_providers.cyrlm.base_url=http://127.0.0.1:11535/v1 -c model_providers.cyrlm.wire_api=responses -c model_provider=cyrlm -c web_search=disabled -c model_context_window=65536 -c model_auto_compact_token_limit=52428 -m qwen3.6:35b-a3b-cyrlm
   then restart: Codex CLI: start a new session in your own terminal

8. Verify the setup
   Checks that llama.cpp (llama-server) answers at http://127.0.0.1:8080 with qwen3.6:35b-a3b-cyrlm, that the context window is 65536 tokens and compares real speed with cyrlm's prediction. It then sends requests in codex's own format (a greeting, a tool call and the tool result) and reports "Ready" only if all three work: a fast runtime can still reject a coding tool's requests. The setup is not done until this says Ready.
     cyrlm verify --runtime llamacpp --endpoint http://127.0.0.1:8080 --model qwen3.6:35b-a3b-cyrlm --catalog-model qwen3.6-35b-a3b --quant Q4_K_M --ctx 65536 --harness codex

⚠ The model download is 22.1 GB; keep at least 26.3 GB of disk space free.
